The next work is to unify these into one general candidate-selection and validation study.
>
> ## Key Implementation Changes
>
> - Refactor the S-parameter study into one primary workflow:
>
>   - `inventory`: discover `.s2p` / `.s4p`, ignore `__MACOSX` metadata files, record port count, frequency span, points, Z0, SHA-256, dominant paths, and duplicate groups.
>   - `qualify`: convert candidates, run HSPICE-independent checks, select the best ngspice model, and write the final ngspice-ready model.
>   - `audit-hspice`: optional development command that compares the selected model against HSPICE and updates correlation statistics.
>   - `report`: generate CSV/Markdown/PDF-style plots showing independent score vs HSPICE correlation.
> - Candidate model families, all selected by fixed global rules, never per-file hardcoding:
>
>   - Full passive vector-fit model from scikit-rf/SPICE export.
>   - Passivity-enforced full vector-fit variants.
>   - Delay-aware reduced through-path model with RC residual/tail branches.
>   - Reduced model plus input reflection correction.
>   - Reduced model plus zero-DC feedthrough/ringing basis for sharp edge behavior.
>   - For `.s4p`, v1 may use dominant differential/through paths as a reduced approximation, but must clearly label this as `reduced_4p`, not a full 4-port replacement.
> - HSPICE-independent quality score:
>
>   - Frequency-domain fit: complex RMS/max error, magnitude dB error above `-40 dB`, phase/group-delay error on dominant through paths.
>   - Physical sanity: sampled passivity, dense max singular value, causality-like impulse pre-response, high-frequency gain trend, nonfinite checks.
>   - Transient smoke in ngspice only: 50 ohm source/load, ideal source/load, edge rates `5 ps`, `50 ps`, `500 ps`, amplitudes `0.05 V`, `0.1 V`, `0.5 V`, `1.5 V`.
>   - Edge-specific metrics: edge-window RMSE, peak overshoot/undershoot error, ringing peak count/amplitude/timing, settling error, and 50% crossing with early-ring detection so false threshold crossings are classified explicitly.
> - Selection policy:
>
>   - Reject any candidate with nonfinite output, unstable ngspice run, dense max singular value above hard limit, severe passivity violation, nonphysical transient bounds, or large pre-response.
>   - Prefer the lowest-complexity candidate that passes hard gates.
>   - Rank passing candidates by independent score only.
>   - HSPICE correlation must never change selected model during normal qualification; it only evaluates whether the independent score was predictive.
> - Outputs:
>
>   - `manifest.csv`: all discovered channels and metadata.
>   - `metrics.csv`: HSPICE-independent quality metrics per candidate.
>   - `ranking.csv`: selected model, independent score, model family, and reason.
>   - `ngspice_smoke.csv`: ngspice-only transient sanity results.
>   - `hspice_correlation.csv`: optional audit correlation results.
>   - `calibration_summary.csv`: confusion matrix showing independent `PASS/WARN/FAIL` vs HSPICE audit result.
>   - Clear plots: S-parameter fit overlays, singular-value/passivity plots, ngspice smoke plots, and optional HSPICE-vs-ngspice overlays.
>
> ## Validation Strategy
>
> - Use HSPICE only to calibrate trust:
>
>   - Run the optional audit over all available repo-local channels, Cisco channels, Molex, scikit-rf test Touchstones, and future user-supplied folders.
>   - Split data into calibration and holdout groups by source/family so thresholds are not tuned to one channel set.
>   - Track false pass rate as the primary risk metric: independent `PASS` but poor HSPICE agreement.
>   - Promote a threshold set only when holdout false-pass rate is acceptably low and failures are explainable.
> - Initial acceptance gates:
>
>   - Independent `PASS` should predict HSPICE audit `PASS` for at least `95%` of holdout transient cases.
>   - No known unstable/non-passive model can receive independent `PASS`.
>   - Every `WARN` must include a specific reason, such as `edge_ringing_threshold_ambiguous`, `reduced_4p_not_full_matrix`, or `passivity_margin_low`.
>   - Every final selected model must include enough metadata to reproduce the conversion.
>
> ## Test Plan
>
> - Unit-style checks:
>
>   - Inventory excludes `__MACOSX` sidecar files and records duplicates by SHA-256.
>   - Port-count parsing correctly classifies `.s2p`, `.s4p`, and unsupported files.
>   - Independent metrics detect known bad direct vector-fit cases already observed in Cisco runs.
>   - Edge classifier distinguishes true main-edge delay from early ringing threshold crossings.
>   - Candidate selection never reads HSPICE correlation files.
> - Integration checks:
>
>   - Run full qualification on `Clarity_example.S2P`, `ch_model_fit.s2p`, `Molex2006-2_T.s4p`, Cisco channels, and fetched scikit-rf Touchstones.
>   - Verify each selected model has ngspice deck/raw/log outputs and independent metrics.
>   - Verify optional HSPICE audit produces `.tr0`/`.lis`, overlays, and correlation CSVs.
>   - Verify reports clearly show which cases are `PASS`, `WARN`, and `FAIL`.
> - Regression checks:
>
>   - Cisco strong S31 cases should remain high-confidence for RX.
>   - `.s2p` Clarity should show improved feedthrough/ringing behavior versus the no-ring reduced model.
>   - A deliberately non-passive or unstable fit must fail before HSPICE is consulted.
>
> ## Assumptions And Defaults
>
> - v1 target use case is digital transient channel simulation with typical 50 ohm source/load conditions; arbitrary nonlinear driver/receiver and arbitrary terminations are later scope unless the model is a full passive multiport.
> - `.s2p` gets priority for full two-port generalization: S21, S11, then S12/S22 behavior.
> - `.s4p` v1 can continue using reduced dominant-path models, but any such model is marked `reduced_4p` and not advertised as a full 4-port S-matrix replacement.
> - HSPICE is available for development audits on this machine, but the final ngspice qualification command must work without HSPICE.
> - No per-channel hand tuning is allowed; all candidate families, hyperparameter grids, and thresholds are global and recorded in the report.

</details>

> explain cleary the latest finding and next steps

Latest finding: the workflow is now structurally right, but the model confidence is still conservative.

The important result is this:

- `qualify` now selects models using only HSPICE-independent checks.
- HSPICE is only used later by `audit-hspice` to test whether the independent confidence label was honest.
- The first calibration exposed exactly the risk we were worried about: `Clarity_example.S2P` looked good by frequency/passivity fit alone, but HSPICE showed fast-edge mismatch.
- After adding ngspice-only edge sanity checks, especially RX overshoot/undershoot, that case is now classified as `WARN`, not `PASS`.

So the latest conclusion is:

`PASS` should mean “we trust ngspice without HSPICE.”
Right now, the new flow correctly avoids calling the known risky fast-edge case a clean `PASS`.

For `Clarity_example.S2P`, the selected vector-fit model is:

- independent class: `WARN`
- reason: `rx_overshoot_margin;rx_undershoot_margin`
- HSPICE audit: 500 ps edge passes, fast 5 ps / 50 ps cases fail

That says the model is probably okay for slower edges, but not yet trustworthy for fast-edge digital transient use.

For `ch_model_fit.s2p`, direct vector-fit candidates failed independent gates before selection because of non-passivity / dense singular value / magnitude error. That is good behavior: the workflow refused to generate confidence from a weak model.

**Next Steps**

1. Add Touchstone-only reduced candidates
   We need the delay-aware / ringing model family, but fitted from Touchstone-derived impulse/step behavior, not HSPICE waveforms. That is the big next move.
2. Run broad calibration
   Run `qualify` + `audit-hspice` across Cisco, Molex, local `.s2p`, scikit-rf tests, and future channels. Track false `PASS` rate.
3. Tune confidence thresholds
   The goal is near-zero false `PASS`. `WARN` is acceptable for ambiguous edge behavior; `PASS` must be strict.
4. Improve `.s4p` handling
   Keep reduced dominant-path models labeled as `reduced_4p`. Do not pretend they are full passive 4-port replacements.
5. Produce final trust report
   The deliverable should show: selected model, independent class, warning/fail reason, ngspice smoke plots, and optional HSPICE calibration evidence.

Short version: we now have the right framework. The next hard part is adding better HSPICE-independent candidate models so more real channels can become true `PASS`, not just `WARN` or `FAIL`.

> what's current conclusion and next steps?

**Current Conclusion**
We now have the right architecture for a trustworthy ngspice flow, but we are not yet at “independent PASS means safe” for broad use.

The good finding: `qualify` is now HSPICE-independent. It selects using Touchstone-derived metrics plus ngspice smoke only. HSPICE is only used afterward by `audit-hspice`.

The important calibration result: for the Cisco `.s4p` smoke case, the new Touchstone-only reduced model was selectable, but only as `WARN`, with scope `matched_50ohm_reduced_4p`. HSPICE audit then showed tiny voltage RMSE but large 50% threshold timing deltas. That means our independent workflow correctly avoided calling it `PASS`.

For `.s2p`, `Clarity_example.S2P` still prefers `vector_3r3c` as `WARN`; the new reduced `.s2p` candidates ran and generated plots, but failed the independent fit gates. So reduced candidates are wired in, but they are not automatically better.

**What This Means**
We are approaching a general workflow, but the current reduced model is still scope-limited:

- Full vector-fit models are still the only candidates eligible for `general_multiport`.
- Reduced `.s4p` is currently a dominant-path model, mainly `p1 -> p3` / S31-style behavior.
- Weak-signal cases are tricky: voltage RMSE can look excellent while threshold timing is unstable or misleading.
- The independent classifier is conservative, which is good. Right now it is producing WARN instead of false PASS.

Useful files:

- [Cisco reduced smoke README](./results/sparam_trust_workflow_reduced_smoke_2026-06-09_d/README.md)
- [S2P smoke README](./results/sparam_trust_workflow_reduced_s2p_smoke_2026-06-09_b/README.md)

**Next Steps**

1. Run a broader calibration batch across Cisco, Molex, repo-local `.s2p/.s4p`, and scikit-rf fixtures.
2. Audit selected calibration cases with HSPICE and build the false-PASS table.
3. Tighten delay metrics for low-swing cases so threshold timing is not over-interpreted.
4. Improve reduced `.s4p` beyond dominant S31 by adding at least S11/S13/S33-style behavior or clearly separating RX-fit confidence from TX/reflection confidence.
5. Promote `PASS` thresholds only after holdout data shows low false-PASS rate.

Bottom line: the framework is now in the right shape. The next real work is calibration volume and model-family improvement, not plumbing.

> so the rx side behavior actually got worse (s31/s21)?

<details><summary>1 previous message</summary>

> I’ll check the actual metrics for selected reduced `.s4p` and the reflected variant before answering, because “worse” can mean RX waveform RMSE, S31/S21 frequency fit, or 50% threshold timing, and those point in different directions.

</details>

Short answer: **not really for RX voltage shape / S31 amplitude**, but **yes if you look at 50% timing or the reflected variant’s transient score**.

For the selected Cisco reduced `.s4p` model, RX is still very close in voltage:

- `rx_active_rmse_v` around `0.00045–0.00050 V`
- `rx_active_maxabs_v` around `0.0012–0.0013 V`

That is quite good. The ugly numbers are the 50% delay deltas, but those are now marked low-confidence because the RX swing is tiny. So the 50% crossing can move by hundreds or thousands of ps without meaning the S31 waveform shape is bad.

What did get worse:

- The new `reduced_4p_dominant_delay_rc_reflect` candidate did not improve things.
- For `Ch10_35_5F3N_f1`, the reflected candidate had the same S31 frequency fit as the non-reflect model, but worse transient shape score:
  - non-reflect `max_voltage_shape_score_v`: about `0.00088 V`
  - reflect `max_voltage_shape_score_v`: about `0.0097 V`
- Because of that, the workflow correctly kept selecting `reduced_4p_dominant_delay_rc`, not the reflected version.

So the finding is:

**S31/S21 RX voltage behavior did not broadly get worse in the selected model. The RX timing metric looks worse because low-swing threshold crossings are unreliable. The reflection-augmented candidate can worsen transient behavior and is not yet useful.**

For `.s2p`, `Clarity_example` is different: its selected full vector model still fails HSPICE RX voltage metrics for faster edges, so S21 there genuinely needs more work.

> Plan
>
> # Plan: Improve ngspice S-parameter Conversion Toward Simulation-Ready Trust
>
> ## Summary
>
> The next phase should split the problem into two goals: make the **RX through path** trustworthy first (`S21` / `S31`), then improve **reflection and interaction behavior** (`S11`, `S33`, crosstalk, TX-side waveform). Current calibration says selected reduced `.s4p` models often match RX voltage shape well, but remain `WARN` because they are reduced-scope and threshold timing is low-confidence. The reflected reduced candidate currently does not improve enough to be selected.
>
> On the “separate simulations then combine” idea: yes, this can be useful as a **qualification and reconstruction tool** for linear, fixed 50 ohm cases, but it should not be the default final ngspice simulation result. We can run separate RX-focused and reflection-focused tests to certify each behavior, and optionally combine wave-domain responses only under strict linear/same-termination assumptions. For general simulation, the final deliverable should still be one consistent ngspice model or a clearly scoped set of models.
>
> ## Key Changes
>
> - Add path-specific qualification views:
>
>   - `rx_through_view`: focuses on `S21` for `.s2p` and `S31` / dominant through path for `.s4p`.
>   - `tx_reflection_view`: focuses on `S11` and TX/input waveform behavior.
>   - `full_model_view`: checks whether one model is safe as a complete multiport replacement.
>   - Output separate trust classes: `rx_trust_class`, `reflection_trust_class`, `full_model_trust_class`.
> - Improve RX-first reduced models:
>
>   - Keep `reduced_4p_dominant_delay_rc` as the RX-through candidate for `.s4p`.
>   - Add RX metrics that ignore invalid low-swing 50% crossings and prioritize waveform RMSE, peak error, settling, and frequency-domain `S31/S21` fit.
>   - Allow an RX-specific `PASS` only for declared scope: `matched_50ohm_rx_through`.
>   - Keep full-model class as `WARN` unless reflection and multiport behavior also pass.
> - Rework reflection modeling:
>
>   - Replace the current reflected reduced candidate with a separate `reflection_view` fit that is judged by `S11` frequency fit and TX waveform correlation, not by whether it improves RX.
>   - Do not let a reflection correction degrade RX-through score.
>   - If reflection and RX models cannot coexist cleanly, emit two scoped models rather than forcing one bad combined model.
> - Add optional linear reconstruction mode:
>
>   - For fixed 50 ohm, linear-only studies, compute a postprocessed reconstructed response from independently fitted through/reflection views.
>   - Label this output `analysis_only_linear_reconstruction`, not a general ngspice-ready model.
>   - Do not use reconstruction for nonlinear drivers, arbitrary terminations, or final user-facing simulation unless validated separately.
> - Broaden calibration reports:
>
>   - Add path-level tables: RX-through PASS/WARN/FAIL, reflection PASS/WARN/FAIL, full-model PASS/WARN/FAIL.
>   - Add HSPICE audit correlation per view, especially whether RX-through trust predicts RX waveform agreement.
>   - Keep false independent `PASS` rate as the headline metric, but compute it separately for RX-through and full-model claims.
>
> ## Implementation Changes
>
> - Update `scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py`:
>
>   - Add view-level metrics and trust columns to `metrics.csv`, `ranking.csv`, and reports.
>   - Add candidate families:
>     - `reduced_s2p_rx_delay_rc_ring`
>     - `reduced_s2p_reflection`
>     - `reduced_4p_rx_dominant_delay_rc`
>     - `reduced_4p_reflection`
>     - optional `linear_reconstructed_rx`
>   - Keep existing `full_vector_fit` candidates for `general_multiport`.
> - Selection policy:
>
>   - Select the best RX-through model for `rx_selected_model`.
>   - Select the best reflection model for `reflection_selected_model`.
>   - Select a `full_selected_model` only if one candidate passes both RX and reflection/full-matrix gates.
>   - Final `selected_model.sp` should be the full model if available; otherwise write scoped selected models under `selected_models/rx/` and `selected_models/reflection/`.
> - Report policy:
>
>   - README must clearly say whether a channel has:
>     - `RX_READY`
>     - `REFLECTION_READY`
>     - `FULL_MODEL_READY`
>     - or only `WARN/FAIL`.
>   - Never advertise a reduced `.s4p` RX model as a full multiport replacement.
>
> ## Test Plan
>
> - Unit-style checks:
>
>   - RX-through trust is computed from `S21/S31` and RX waveform metrics only.
>   - Reflection trust is computed from `S11` and TX/input waveform metrics.
>   - A model with good RX but bad reflection can receive `RX_READY` but not `FULL_MODEL_READY`.
>   - Linear reconstruction is disabled or marked invalid for non-50 ohm / nonlinear setups.
> - Integration checks:
>
>   - Cisco `.s4p`: dominant RX path should often become `RX_READY` or high-confidence `WARN`, while full model remains `WARN`.
>   - `Clarity_example.S2P`: fast-edge RX failures should prevent RX `PASS` until the model improves.
>   - `ntwk2`: validate that current good HSPICE correlation maps to stronger RX trust.
>   - RS_ZNB8: verify TX/reflection failures remain visible and are not hidden by RX fit.
> - Calibration acceptance:
>
>   - RX-through independent `PASS` must predict HSPICE RX waveform pass for at least 95% of audited holdout cases.
>   - Full-model `PASS` remains stricter and requires reflection/TX behavior to pass too.
>   - Any false RX `PASS` must produce a named missing metric before thresholds are promoted.
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> - Primary user value is reliable RX waveform simulation, so `S21/S31` gets priority.
> - Reflection behavior is still important, but should not block scoped RX-through qualification if clearly labeled.
> - Separate simulation/reconstruction is allowed only as an analysis aid under linear fixed-termination assumptions.
> - Final ngspice-ready deliverables must be honest about scope: RX-through model, reflection model, or full multiport model.

</details>

> so think, is this really the right direction?

Yes, but only as a **trust framework**, not as the final modeling strategy by itself.

The right part is splitting claims:

- `RX_READY`: “I trust S21/S31 for matched 50 ohm RX waveform use.”
- `REFLECTION_READY`: “I trust S11/TX-side behavior.”
- `FULL_MODEL_READY`: “I trust this as a real multiport replacement.”

That is the right direction because our earlier mistake was treating one reduced S31/S21 model like it answered every question. It did not. The new split keeps us honest.

But the risk is: we could spend too much time polishing labels/metrics while the actual ngspice model still lacks the physics of the full S-matrix. So the direction is right only if we use it to guide model improvement.

My current take:

1. RX-first is sensible.
   Most value is probably RX waveform accuracy. A reduced S31/S21 model can be useful and often close to HSPICE for matched cases.
2. It should not become the final general answer.
   A path-only model cannot be trusted for arbitrary terminations, nonlinear drivers, reflections, crosstalk, or full 4-port behavior.
3. Separate simulations can help qualification, but not replace a full model.
   We can run an RX-focused sim and an S11-focused sim to measure confidence. We can even reconstruct linear 50 ohm responses offline. But combining separate results is only valid under strict linear/fixed-termination assumptions. It is not a general ngspice simulation flow.
4. The real next technical target should be model quality.
   The trust framework should tell us which model family fails: full vector fit, RX reduced, reflection reduced, etc. Then we improve the model family, especially full passive multiport fitting and reflection-aware reduced models.

So my answer is: **yes, this is the right direction as a scaffolding**, because it prevents false confidence. But the real success condition is not more classification; it is eventually getting more channels to `RX_READY`, then `FULL_MODEL_READY`, with HSPICE audits proving the independent metrics predict reality.

> so what's next? be detailed and think through

Next, I would stop adding more labels and use the labels to drive model work. The path split is useful, but now we need to make it earn trust.

**1. Run a real baseline with the new view-level flow**
Use the new `rx/reflection/full` reporting over all available channels, then audit a meaningful subset with HSPICE.

Goal: answer these separately:

- Does independent `rx_trust_class` predict HSPICE RX agreement?
- Does independent `reflection_trust_class` predict TX/S11 agreement?
- Are any independent `PASS` cases false passes?
- Which warning reasons are real blockers vs overly conservative?

This should produce the first serious calibration table.

**2. Tighten the RX claim**
Right now Cisco RX is `WARN`, not because voltage shape is bad, but because the RX swing is tiny and 50% timing is unreliable. I think we should split RX into two internal subclaims:

- `rx_voltage_shape_trust`: RMSE, max error, settling, overshoot.
- `rx_timing_trust`: 50% delay only when swing/crossing confidence is good.

Then `RX_READY` should mean both are good, but low-swing channels can become something like “RX voltage shape ready, timing ambiguous.” That is more honest than forcing everything into one 50% delay metric.

**3. Improve the actual S21/S31 model**
For RX-through, the next modeling improvement should be delay-aware fitting, not just more RC branches.

Many channels are basically:

```text
pure delay + frequency-dependent loss + small ringing
```

Regular vector fitting wastes model order trying to represent delay. Better workflow:

1. Estimate dominant delay from S21/S31 group delay or impulse peak.
2. Remove delay from the Touchstone path: fit `S21(f) * exp(+jωτ)`.
3. Fit the residual with a stable/passive rational or reduced RC/ringing basis.
4. Reinsert delay explicitly in the ngspice model.

That should improve fast-edge behavior without exploding model order.

**4. Rework reflection separately**
The current reflection candidate is weak. It should not be judged by whether it improves RX. It should be judged by:

- S11 frequency fit.
- TX-side ngspice smoke waveform.
- HSPICE TX correlation during audit.

If S11 is small and TX waveform is insensitive, reflection can be `WARN` with a named reason. If S11 is large, it needs a real reflection model before we can claim full trust.

**5. Do not combine separate sims as the main answer**
Separate RX and reflection simulations are useful for qualification and debugging. But combining them afterward is only valid for linear, fixed 50 ohm cases. It should remain `analysis_only_linear_reconstruction`.

For final user simulation, we still want either:

- a scoped RX-through model, clearly labeled, or
- a real full multiport model.

**6. Next concrete implementation**
I would implement these next:

- Add `rx_voltage_shape_class` and `rx_timing_class`.
- Promote low-swing RX cases from vague `WARN` to a specific `rx_timing_ambiguous_voltage_shape_ok`.
- Add delay-removal/reinserted-delay candidates for `.s2p` and `.s4p` dominant paths.
- Improve reflection fitting as its own candidate family.
- Run full qualification + HSPICE audit and compare false-pass rates by view.

The main success target should be: **RX-through independent PASS predicts HSPICE RX PASS on holdout cases, with near-zero false passes.** Only after that should we chase `FULL_MODEL_READY`.

> # Plan: Make RX-First ngspice S-parameter Conversion Trustworthy
>
> ## Summary
>
> The view split is the right scaffold, but the next work must shift from labels to model improvement and calibration. We will make RX-through behavior the first trustworthy deliverable, keep reflection/full-model claims separate, and use HSPICE only to prove whether the HSPICE-independent metrics predict simulator agreement.
>
> Current state to preserve:
>
> - Cisco reduced `.s4p` RX/S31 models often match RX voltage shape very well, but remain `WARN` because threshold timing is low-confidence.
> - Reflection remains independently weak because S11 frequency fit fails, even when one HSPICE TX waveform audit happens to look acceptable.
> - Reduced `.s4p` models must never be advertised as full multiport replacements.
>
> ## Implementation Changes
>
> - Add RX sub-classes in `scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py`:
>
>   - `rx_voltage_shape_class`: based on RX waveform RMSE/max error, settling, overshoot, pre-response, and RX S21/S31 fit.
>   - `rx_timing_class`: based on 50% delay only when RX swing and threshold crossings are high-confidence.
>   - `rx_ready_status` becomes `RX_READY` only when voltage shape and timing both pass; otherwise use named WARN states such as `RX_VOLTAGE_OK_TIMING_AMBIGUOUS`.
> - Add delay-equalized RX candidate families:
>
>   - `reduced_s2p_rx_delayeq_rc_ring`
>   - `reduced_4p_rx_delayeq_rc_ring`
>   - Estimate dominant delay from Touchstone using impulse peak plus group-delay median.
>   - Remove delay from S21/S31, fit the residual with the existing RC/tail/ringing basis, then reinsert delay explicitly in ngspice.
>   - Score against both frequency-domain S21/S31 and Touchstone-derived 5 ps / 50 ps / 500 ps step responses.
> - Rework reflection as its own model family:
>
>   - `reduced_s2p_reflection_s11_rc`
>   - `reduced_4p_reflection_s11_rc`
>   - Judge these only by S11 frequency fit and TX/input waveform smoke metrics.
>   - Do not allow reflection correction to degrade RX selection.
>   - Add combined RX+reflection candidates only if both individual views pass and RX score degradation stays below a fixed global threshold.
> - Extend outputs:
>
>   - `metrics.csv`: add delay estimate, delay estimator source, RX voltage/timing classes, S11 reflection fit metrics, and candidate view role.
>   - `ranking.csv`: keep `rx_selected_*`, `reflection_selected_*`, `full_selected_*`, plus best-attempt failure reasons for each view.
>   - `hspice_correlation.csv`: add `rx_shape_hspice_audit_class`, `rx_timing_hspice_audit_class`, and `reflection_hspice_audit_class`.
>   - `README.md`: show RX voltage/timing readiness separately from full-model readiness.
> - Keep separate simulation/reconstruction analysis-only:
>
>   - Implement or retain `linear_reconstructed_rx` only as `analysis_only_linear_reconstruction`.
>   - Never use reconstructed separate simulations as the default final ngspice model.
>   - Permit it only for fixed 50 ohm, linear, postprocessed studies.
>
> ## Calibration Workflow
>
> - Run full qualification after implementation:
>
>   ```powershell
>   py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py qualify `
>     --study-dir results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-10 `
>     --skrf-target "$env:TEMP\ibis_skrf_target" `
>     --skrf-tests-dir results/sparam_conversion_quality_2026-06-08/inputs/skrf_tests `
>     --extra-touchstone-dir hspice/sparam `
>     --fast-calibration-profile `
>     --dense-samples 501 `
>     --sim-timeout 180
>   ```
> - Run HSPICE audit after qualification:
>
>   ```powershell
>   py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py audit-hspice `
>     --study-dir results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-10 `
>     --skrf-target "$env:TEMP\ibis_skrf_target" `
>     --sim-timeout 240 `
>     --audit-stop-ns 35 `
>     --resume
>   ```
> - Calibration acceptance:
>
>   - `RX_READY` false-pass rate on audited holdout cases must be below 5%.
>   - No known unstable, non-passive, nonfinite, or severe pre-response case may receive `RX_READY` or `FULL_MODEL_READY`.
>   - `FULL_MODEL_READY` requires a general multiport candidate; reduced `.s4p` can only reach scoped RX/reflection readiness.
>   - Any false `RX_READY` must produce a named missing metric before thresholds are promoted.
>
> ## Test Plan
>
> - Unit-style checks:
>
>   - Delay estimation is deterministic and finite for `.s2p` and `.s4p`.
>   - Delay removal reduces dominant-path group-delay variation on delayed channels.
>   - Low RX swing produces timing WARN, not voltage-shape FAIL.
>   - Good RX / bad reflection can become RX-scoped ready or WARN, but never full ready.
>   - Candidate selection does not read HSPICE correlation files.
> - Integration checks:
>
>   - Cisco Ch10 `.s4p`: RX voltage shape should remain strong; timing should remain WARN if low-swing threshold confidence is poor.
>   - `Clarity_example.S2P`: fast-edge RX mismatch must not become false `RX_READY`.
>   - Known good `ntwk2` cases: should move toward stronger RX readiness if independent metrics and HSPICE agree.
>   - RS_ZNB8-like cases: reflection/TX weakness must stay visible.
>   - Molex and scikit-rf fixtures: all produce manifest, metrics, ranking, scoped selected models, and plots.
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> - Primary v1 value is reliable matched-50-ohm RX waveform simulation.
> - S21 is the default `.s2p` RX path; S31 is the default `.s4p` RX path for the current HSPICE/ngspice bench convention.
> - Reflection is important, but it should not block a clearly scoped RX-through claim.
> - No per-channel tuning is allowed; all candidate grids, thresholds, and readiness rules are global and recorded in output metadata.
> - HSPICE remains audit-only and never affects `qualify` selection.

Implemented the RX-first trust upgrade in [run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py](./scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py).

What changed:

- Added RX sub-classes: `rx_voltage_shape_class` and `rx_timing_class`.
- Changed `rx_ready_status` so `RX_READY` requires both voltage shape and timing to pass.
- Added named WARN states like `RX_WARN_VOLTAGE_MARGIN` and timing-ambiguous behavior.
- Added delay-equalized candidates:
  - `reduced_s2p_rx_delayeq_rc_ring`
  - `reduced_4p_rx_delayeq_rc_ring`
- Added S11-specific reflection candidates:
  - `reduced_s2p_reflection_s11_rc`
  - `reduced_4p_reflection_s11_rc`
- Added Touchstone-only delay metadata: step threshold, impulse peak, group-delay median, estimator source.
- Added HSPICE audit split fields:
  - `rx_shape_hspice_audit_class`
  - `rx_timing_hspice_audit_class`
  - existing `rx_hspice_audit_class` now combines those.
- Added conservative combined-candidate gating so RX+reflection combined models cannot be selected unless individual RX and reflection views are already good and RX shape degradation is below a fixed global threshold.

Verified:

- `py -3.14 -m py_compile scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py` passed.
- Cisco smoke: `results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_cisco_smoke_2026-06-10`
  - RX remains scoped `WARN`, reflection `FAIL`, full model `WARN`.
  - Delay-equalized candidates are generated and recorded, but not selected in that smoke.
- S2P smoke: `results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_s2p_smoke_2026-06-10`
  - `Clarity_example` remains not `RX_READY`: `RX_WARN_VOLTAGE_MARGIN`.
  - RX shape is `WARN`, RX timing is `PASS`, reflection is `FAIL`.
- HSPICE audit on the S2P smoke produced the new split audit columns.

Current status: we made real progress, but we are still in **qualification/calibration**, not “ngspice is trusted broadly” yet.

**What is now working**
The pipeline now separates the claims we care about:

- `rx_voltage_shape_class`: is the RX waveform shape sane?
- `rx_timing_class`: is 50% timing meaningful and trustworthy?
- `rx_ready_status`: only becomes `RX_READY` if both shape and timing pass.
- `reflection_trust_class`: separate S11/TX-side confidence.
- `full_model_trust_class`: strict full-model claim.

That is a big improvement because we are no longer mixing “RX looks good” with “this is a full S-parameter replacement.”

**Latest verified results**
Cisco smoke:
`results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_cisco_smoke_2026-06-10`

- 2 Cisco `.s4p` cases ran.
- Selected model: `reduced_4p_rx_dominant_delay_rc`
- RX: `WARN`
- RX voltage shape: `WARN`
- RX timing: `WARN`
- Reflection: `FAIL`
- Full model: `WARN`

Interpretation: Cisco RX still looks useful, but we are not calling it ready because timing is low-confidence and S11/reflection is not modeled well enough.

S2P / Clarity smoke:
`results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_s2p_smoke_2026-06-10`

- `Clarity_example` selected `vector_3r3c`.
- RX status: `RX_WARN_VOLTAGE_MARGIN`
- RX shape: `WARN`
- RX timing: `PASS`
- Reflection: `FAIL`
- HSPICE audit confirms the warning was meaningful:
  - Fast edges failed RX shape vs HSPICE.
  - 500 ps edge passed RX shape.
  - Timing mostly matched, with one timing WARN.

That is exactly the behavior we want from the metric: it did **not** falsely call Clarity `RX_READY`.

**Important finding**
The new split is already useful:

- Cisco problem is mostly “low-swing/timing confidence + reflection not ready.”
- Clarity problem is “RX voltage shape is not good enough on fast edges, even though timing looks okay.”
- So the weak point is not one universal thing. The workflow is now capable of telling us *what kind* of weakness we have.

**What is not done yet**
We have not run the full v2 calibration sweep over all available channels. Also, the new delay-equalized candidates are being generated, but in the smoke cases they did not beat the existing selected models yet. So the modeling improvement is present structurally, but not proven as better.

**Best next steps for today, June 11, 2026**
The goal by end of day should be a clear calibration report, not a final claim that ngspice is solved.

1. Run the full HSPICE-independent qualification sweep.

```powershell
py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py qualify `
  --study-dir results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11 `
  --skrf-target "$env:TEMP\ibis_skrf_target" `
  --skrf-tests-dir results/sparam_conversion_quality_2026-06-08/inputs/skrf_tests `
  --extra-touchstone-dir hspice/sparam `
  --fast-calibration-profile `
  --dense-samples 501 `
  --sim-timeout 180
```

2. Inspect `view_trust_summary.csv` and `ranking.csv`.
   We want counts for:

   - RX_READY
   - RX voltage WARN vs timing WARN
   - reflection FAIL
   - full-model WARN/FAIL
3. Run a limited HSPICE audit, not the whole universe yet.
   Use representative selected cases first, enough to show whether the metric is predictive.

```powershell
py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py audit-hspice `
  --study-dir results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11 `
  --skrf-target "$env:TEMP\ibis_skrf_target" `
  --sim-timeout 240 `
  --audit-stop-ns 35 `
  --max-channels 10 `
  --resume
```

4. Regenerate the report.

```powershell
py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py report `
  --study-dir results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11
```

**End-of-day deliverable**
By EOD, we should have:

- One canonical result folder: `results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11`
- A README that clearly says how many channels are RX ready/warn/fail.
- HSPICE overlay PDFs for audited cases.
- A short conclusion table:
  - cases where independent RX WARN correctly predicted HSPICE issue,
  - cases where RX shape passed,
  - cases where timing is ambiguous,
  - cases where reflection is still blocking full-model trust.

That would be real visible progress: not “we fixed everything,” but “we now have a calibrated, evidence-based path to knowing when ngspice can be trusted.”

Current headline result:

- Channels inventoried: 226
- Supported channels processed: 205
- Selected channels: 149
- Overall independent PASS/WARN/FAIL: 0 / 147 / 2
- RX voltage-shape PASS/WARN/FAIL: 7 / 142 / 56
- RX timing PASS/WARN/FAIL: 4 / 145 / 56
- Combined RX_READY: 0
- Reflection PASS/WARN/FAIL: 0 / 2 / 203
- Full-model PASS/WARN/FAIL: 0 / 149 / 56
- HSPICE correlation rows: 60
- Successful HSPICE correlations: 47

The important finding is: the new workflow is conservative, which is good for trust building. There are no false `RX_READY` claims because nothing is yet promoted to combined RX ready. The most promising signal is RX voltage shape: 3 audited independent RX-shape PASS cases all matched HSPICE shape PASS, so false-pass rate for audited RX-shape PASS is currently 0. Timing is weaker: independent timing PASS sometimes maps to HSPICE WARN, so timing confidence still needs work.

Reflection/full-model readiness is still the weak point. Reduced `.s4p` models are correctly not being reported as full multiport replacements. That rule held.

Next highest-value work:

1. Investigate the 13 HSPICE audit error rows so the audit coverage is cleaner.
2. Audit targeted channels next, not just the first 20: all RX-shape PASS cases, delay-equalized selections, and `RX_VOLTAGE_OK_TIMING_AMBIGUOUS` cases.
3. Rework reflection scoring so we distinguish “S11/full reflection model is bad” from “TX observable in this 50 ohm bench still correlates.”
4. Extend the same audit to 40 channels with `--max-channels 40 --resume`.

So yes: this produced clear progress for today. We now have a canonical v2 report that separates RX shape, RX timing, reflection, and full-model readiness, with HSPICE audit evidence instead of hand impressions.

I created the canonical study here:

[results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11/README.md](./results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11/README.md)

The workflow had two phases:

1. **ngspice-only qualification**

   - Scanned available `.s2p` / `.s4p` files from repo, Cisco, Molex, and scikit-rf test channels.
   - Converted candidates to ngspice-compatible models.
   - Judged them without HSPICE using:
     - RX through behavior, mostly `S21` / `S31`
     - RX voltage shape
     - RX 50% timing
     - reflection / `S11`
     - full-model readiness
2. **HSPICE audit**

   - Took the first 20 selected channels.
   - Ran HSPICE as the reference.
   - Compared ngspice waveform overlays against HSPICE.
   - Generated overlay PDFs here:

[audit_overlay_groups](./results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11/audit_overlay_groups)

**Main Results**

We processed:

- 226 Touchstone files discovered
- 205 supported for this v1 flow
- 149 channels got selected ngspice models
- 56 failed qualification

But the important finding is:

**No channel is cleanly `RX_READY` yet.**

That sounds disappointing, but it is actually useful. The workflow is being conservative instead of giving false confidence.

Breakdown:

- RX voltage shape: `7 PASS`, `142 WARN`, `56 FAIL`
- RX timing: `4 PASS`, `145 WARN`, `56 FAIL`
- Combined RX readiness: `0 RX_READY`
- Reflection: mostly `FAIL`
- Full model: `0 FULL_MODEL_READY`

**What This Means**

The RX waveform **shape** is the most promising part. Some cases look good independently, and among the audited RX-shape PASS cases, HSPICE agreed so far. That is good progress.

The RX **timing** is still weaker. Many cases have low swing, ringing, or ambiguous 50% crossings, so the script refuses to call them truly ready.

Reflection / `S11` is still the biggest weak point. Our current independent reflection metric says most cases fail, even though some HSPICE TX-side waveforms look okay. That tells me the reflection scoring is probably too strict or not measuring the same thing as the HSPICE bench waveform.

**Bottom Line**

We now have a real calibration report. It shows:

- RX through-path shape is improving and may become trustworthy first.
- Timing still needs better confidence handling.
- Reflection/full-model behavior is not ready.
- Reduced `.s4p` models are correctly not being advertised as full multiport replacements.

Next, I would inspect the audit error rows, then audit targeted cases instead of just the first 20: all RX-shape PASS cases, delay-equalized cases, and the ambiguous timing cases. That will tell us whether we can safely promote some models to scoped `RX_READY`.

I went ahead and made the audit flow more useful, then ran the targeted follow-up audits.

**What I Changed**

I updated [scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py](./scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py) so `audit-hspice` can now target specific subsets:

- `--rx-voltage-shape-class PASS`
- `--selected-family reduced_4p_rx_delayeq_rc_ring`
- `--channel-id ...`
- `--retry-errors`

I also added `/.codex_deps/` to [.gitignore](./.gitignore) because I had to install a local scikit-rf copy there to run the audit reliably.

**What I Ran**

I audited two important groups:

1. All channels where independent RX voltage shape was `PASS`.
2. All selected `reduced_4p_rx_delayeq_rc_ring` channels.

Updated report:

[README.md](./results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11/README.md)

**Updated Results**

HSPICE audit rows increased from 60 to 93.

- Successful waveform correlations: 80
- Remaining HSPICE error rows: 13
- RX voltage-shape independent `PASS`: 21 audited rows
- HSPICE RX-shape result for those 21 rows: 21 PASS / 0 WARN / 0 FAIL
- Holdout RX-shape PASS rows: 3 / 3 HSPICE PASS

That is the best result so far. It means our independent RX voltage-shape metric is currently predictive on the audited set.

For the delay-equalized `.s4p` reduced model family:

- 15 audited rows
- RX shape: 15 / 15 HSPICE PASS
- Overall audit class: still WARN because timing remains low-confidence

So the delay-equalized reduced models look good for RX waveform shape, but not enough to call them fully `RX_READY`.

**Current Conclusion**

We have real progress on **RX voltage shape**. For scoped matched-50-ohm RX behavior, the independent metric is matching HSPICE very well so far.

But we still should not claim full readiness:

- Combined `RX_READY`: still 0
- RX timing: still mostly WARN due low swing / ambiguous threshold crossings
- Reflection: still weak independently
- Full model: still not ready
- Reduced `.s4p` models remain RX-scoped only, not full multiport replacements

The remaining 13 audit errors are HSPICE-side missing `.tr0` cases, concentrated in five Cisco channels. Ngspice produced outputs; HSPICE `.lis` was zero bytes / no `.tr0`, so this looks like native HSPICE S-element timeout behavior on those large channels, not an ngspice waveform mismatch.

> ok so what should be the next things now, again, we want solid visible result tomorrow to show.

For tomorrow, I would **not** try to “solve all S-parameters.” The strongest visible story is:

> We can now identify scoped RX waveform-shape models that match HSPICE very well, while still honestly warning that timing/reflection/full-model behavior is not ready.

That is a solid, defensible result.

**Tomorrow’s Target Deliverable**
A clean report/slide-ready folder showing:

- RX voltage-shape metric predicts HSPICE: currently `21/21` audited RX-shape PASS rows matched HSPICE PASS.
- Delay-equalized `.s4p` reduced models also look strong for RX shape: `15/15` RX-shape HSPICE PASS.
- Timing is still WARN, not hidden.
- Reflection/full-model readiness is still not ready.
- Clear overlays showing good RX matches and bad/ambiguous cases.

**Next Things To Do**

1. **Make the result visually obvious**
   Generate a compact “demo report” with 6-10 representative overlays:

   - 2-3 RX-shape PASS Cisco cases
   - 2 delay-equalized `.s4p` cases
   - 1 holdout RX-shape PASS case
   - 1 Clarity `.s2p` fast-edge mismatch
   - 1 timing-ambiguous case
   - 1 reflection/full-model weak case

   The figure titles should say:
   `Independent: RX shape PASS, timing WARN | HSPICE: RX shape PASS, timing WARN`
2. **Add a small headline table**
   Something like:

   ```text
   RX voltage-shape PASS audit: 21 / 21 HSPICE PASS
   Holdout RX-shape PASS audit: 3 / 3 HSPICE PASS
   Delay-equalized reduced .s4p: 15 / 15 RX-shape PASS
   Combined RX_READY: 0, because timing remains ambiguous
   FULL_MODEL_READY: 0
   ```
3. **Retry the 13 HSPICE error rows only if time allows**
   These are HSPICE missing `.tr0` cases, probably timeout/native S-element pain. Useful to clean up, but not central to the demo. I would retry with longer timeout, but stop if it burns too much time.
4. **Create a scoped status name**
   Right now “0 RX_READY” sounds too negative. We should introduce a truthful intermediate label:

   `RX_SHAPE_READY_TIMING_WARN`

   Meaning: “RX waveform shape is validated for matched 50 ohm use, but threshold timing is not certified.”

   That matches what the data actually says.
5. **Do not promote full model claims**
   Tomorrow’s message should be explicit:

   - This is not a full 4-port replacement yet.
   - This is not arbitrary termination-ready.
   - This is a scoped matched-50-ohm RX-through result.
   - Reflection and timing are next calibration targets.

**My Recommended Tomorrow Story**

“Yesterday we had scattered HSPICE/ngspice comparisons. Today we built a qualification flow that separates RX shape, RX timing, reflection, and full-model readiness. The strongest result is RX voltage shape: every independently predicted RX-shape PASS case audited so far matched HSPICE. The tool is conservative: it refuses to call the model RX_READY because timing is still ambiguous. That is progress because the tool is starting to know what it can and cannot trust.”

That is the right story to show. It is honest, visible, and it points directly to the next engineering step.

For the current S-parameter trust/audit study, the bench is a simple matched 50 ohm linear pulse bench, not an IBIS-driver bench.

Input stream:

```spice
Vin   src  0   PWL(0 0 1n 0 1n+edge 1.5 9n 1.5 9n+edge 0)
Rsrc  src  p1  50
.tran 10p 35n
```

We run three edge rates: `5 ps`, `50 ps`, and `500 ps`, all at `1.5 V`, with a 50 ohm series source.

For `.s2p`:

```spice
p1 = driven/input side
p2 = RX/load side

ngspice: Xchannel p1 p2 s_equivalent
HSPICE:  Schannel p1 p2 0 MNAME=ch_model
Rterm p2 0 50
```

So TX comparison is `V(p1)`, RX comparison is `V(p2)`.

For `.s4p`:

```spice
p1 = driven/input port
p2 = near-side other port, terminated
p3 = RX/output port
p4 = far-side other port, terminated

ngspice: Xchannel p1 p2 p3 p4 s_equivalent
HSPICE:  Schannel p1 p2 p3 p4 0 MNAME=ch_model

Rnear_neg p2 0 50
Rterm_pos p3 0 50
Rterm_neg p4 0 50
```

So for our current convention, the important RX path is `p1 -> p3`, i.e. roughly `S31`. TX-side comparison is `V(p1)`, RX-side comparison is `V(p3)`.

HSPICE uses the original Touchstone through its native S-element with `Z0=50`, rational fitting, hybrid interpolation, and passivity enabled. ngspice uses the converted SPICE macromodel. Same source, same terminations, same transient setup. That is why the plots are a clean ngspice-converted-model vs HSPICE-native-Touchstone audit.

Almost, but not quite.

The reduced models **do use scikit-rf to read the Touchstone file** and expose the S-parameter data as a `Network` object: frequency array, S-matrix, port count, Z0, etc.

But the reduced models **do not use scikit-rf vector fitting** and **do not use scikit-rf SPICE export**. The reduced-model conversion itself is our custom flow:

`Touchstone -> scikit-rf Network -> extract S21/S31 or S11 -> custom time-domain/RC/ringing fit -> custom .sp subckt`

So the clean distinction is:

- **Full vector-fit model**: scikit-rf `VectorFitting` + scikit-rf SPICE export.
- **Reduced model**: scikit-rf parser only; fitting and `.sp` generation are custom.

I added this clarification to [REPORT_PRESENTATION.md](./results/sparam_rx_trust_v2_2026-06-11/REPORT_PRESENTATION.md).

> so current finding suggest reduced model perform better? explain clearly their similarities and differences

Yes, for the **current RX-through matched-50-ohm use case**, the reduced models are performing better than the full vector-fit models in the cases we care about most, especially the Cisco `.s4p` RX side.

But that statement needs scope:

**Reduced models perform better for RX voltage shape under our fixed 50 ohm bench.**
They do **not** yet solve reflection, arbitrary loading, or full multiport behavior.

**Similarity**

Both model types start from the same Touchstone S-parameter data.

Both produce an ngspice `.sp` subcircuit named `s_equivalent`.

Both are tested in the same bench:

```spice
Vin + Rsrc = 50 ohm source
channel model
50 ohm terminations
.tran pulse test
```

Both are judged by:

- frequency-domain fit
- passivity/stability sanity
- ngspice transient smoke tests
- optional HSPICE audit overlays

**Full Vector-Fit Model**

Flow:

```text
Touchstone -> scikit-rf Network -> scikit-rf VectorFitting -> scikit-rf SPICE export
```

It tries to model the full S-parameter matrix. For `.s2p`, that means S11/S21/S12/S22. For `.s4p`, in principle it means the full 4-port behavior.

Strengths:

- More general conceptually.
- Can eventually support arbitrary terminations and full multiport interaction.
- Only this family can honestly become `FULL_MODEL_READY`.

Weaknesses found so far:

- Good frequency fit does not guarantee good fast-edge transient behavior.
- Some fits fail passivity/stability gates.
- Some correlate poorly with HSPICE at fast edges.
- Higher-order fits can become fragile in ngspice.

**Reduced Model**

Flow:

```text
Touchstone -> scikit-rf Network -> extract S21/S31 path -> custom delay/RC/ringing fit -> custom SPICE subckt
```

It focuses on one behavior first: RX through-path response.

For `.s2p`, that is mainly `S21`.
For `.s4p`, that is mainly `S31` in our bench convention.

Strengths:

- Better aligned with the current goal: reproduce RX waveform shape.
- Less fragile than full matrix vector-fit in several `.s4p` cases.
- Delay + RC/tail/ringing terms give intuitive control over edge and settling behavior.
- Current audit shows RX voltage-shape PASS is predictive: `21/21` audited independent PASS rows also passed HSPICE RX-shape audit.

Weaknesses:

- It is scoped, not general.
- Reduced `.s4p` is not a full 4-port replacement.
- It does not fully model S11/reflection yet.
- It cannot claim arbitrary termination correctness.
- Timing is often still WARN because low swing or ringing makes 50% crossings ambiguous.

**Current Finding**

The reduced model is currently the better practical path for:

```text
matched 50 ohm RX-through transient prediction
```

The full vector-fit model remains the better long-term path for:

```text
general full S-parameter replacement
```

So our direction is not “reduced replaces vector-fit.” It is:

1. Use reduced models to get trustworthy RX-through results first.
2. Keep the scope label honest: `matched_50ohm_rx_through`.
3. Continue improving full vector-fit or another full-matrix approach for true full-model readiness.
4. Improve reflection/S11 separately so TX-side and loading behavior stop being the weak point.

Short answer: **no, not thoroughly enough to conclude “vector fitting cannot work.”**

What we have proven is narrower:

- The **simple/default scikit-rf vector-fit path** is not reliable enough yet as the only ngspice conversion workflow.
- Frequency-domain fit alone is not enough to predict fast-edge transient agreement.
- Reduced RX-through models currently look better for the **scoped matched-50-ohm RX waveform task**.

But we have **not** done a full vector-fitting campaign.

In the canonical v2 run, the CSVs show:

- `full_vector_fit`: `40` candidate rows
- `full_vector_fit_enforced`: `27` candidate rows
- selected full vector-fit channels: `4`
- most Cisco `.s4p` channels were handled by reduced RX-through candidates, not full `.s4p` vector-fit candidates

So the honest conclusion is:

> Reduced models currently perform better for our RX-through 50 ohm bench, but full vector fitting has not been exhausted. It remains the right long-term path for real full multiport replacement.

A thorough vector-fit study should still be done with:

- `.s2p` and `.s4p` full-matrix fits
- higher/lower pole sweeps
- passivity enforcement variants
- path-weighted fitting, especially S21/S31 and S11
- frequency trimming/windowing
- DC extrapolation choices
- separate fast-edge transient audit
- ngspice numerical option sweeps

> so where did the idea of the reduced model method came from?

The reduced-model idea came from the problem shape we observed, not from scikit-rf directly.

The reasoning was:

1. The channel is linear.
2. Our current bench is fixed: 50 ohm source, 50 ohm load/terminations.
3. For RX comparison, we mostly care about one dominant path:
   - `.s2p`: `S21`
   - `.s4p`: `S31` in our bench convention
4. HSPICE vs ngspice differences were most visible at fast edges.
5. Full vector fitting was sometimes fragile or misleading: good frequency fit did not always mean good transient edge behavior.

So the reduced model is basically a targeted linear time-domain approximation:

```text
dominant S-parameter path
  -> estimate delay
  -> fit residual step response using RC/tail/ringing basis
  -> write that as a simple SPICE subcircuit
```

The core idea comes from standard linear-systems intuition:

```text
frequency response H(f)
<-> impulse response h(t)
<-> step response y(t)
```

If we only need matched 50 ohm RX-through behavior, we do not necessarily need to model the whole S-matrix first. We can model the observed through-path response directly.

The structure was chosen because it maps naturally into SPICE:

- **explicit delay**: captures bulk flight time
- **RC low-pass branches**: capture bandwidth-limited edge shaping
- **fast/slow tail pairs**: capture settling tails without permanently changing DC gain
- **ring/feedthrough pairs**: capture sharp-edge bumps/ringing with near-zero DC effect
- **50 ohm output stage**: matches the fixed bench scope

So the reduced model is not a new universal S-parameter theory. It is a pragmatic scoped model:

```text
For this fixed 50 ohm transient bench, can we reproduce the RX waveform better and more robustly than a fragile full vector fit?
```

That is also why we label it honestly:

```text
matched_50ohm_rx_through
```

not:

```text
general_multiport
```

In short: the idea came from treating the channel as a linear filter for the specific RX path, then building a SPICE-friendly approximation of that filter’s time-domain step response.

> # Plan: Dedicated scikit-rf Vector Fitting Campaign
>
> ## Summary
>
> Run a focused experiment to determine whether the scikit-rf `VectorFitting` path can become a trustworthy ngspice full-model workflow. The current v2 study only tried a small vector-fit slice, mostly `.s2p`; this campaign will explicitly sweep vector-fit settings on `.s2p` and `.s4p`, compare against reduced models and HSPICE, and produce clear pass/fail evidence.

> ## Assumptions And Defaults

> - scikit-rf `VectorFitting.vector_fit()` has no direct path-weight argument, so this v1 campaign will not claim true path-weighted fitting.

> - `parameter_type='s'` is used for all exported ngspice `.sp` models.
> - The main target for vector fitting is `general_multiport`; RX-only success is recorded but does not imply full readiness.
> - Reduced models are included only as a baseline comparison, not as vector-fit candidates.

> so what's the finding telling us and what're next steps?

The new vector-fitting pilot is telling us something pretty clear, but still early:

The simple scikit-rf vector-fit path is **not enough yet**, especially for fast edges and `.s4p` channels.

For the three-channel pilot:

- **Clarity `.s2p`**

  - Raw `vector_3r3c` fits and exports correctly.
  - ngspice runs successfully.
  - Independent smoke downgrades it to `WARN` because of RX overshoot/undershoot.
  - HSPICE audit:
    - `5 ps`: FAIL
    - `50 ps`: FAIL
    - `500 ps`: PASS
  - Meaning: vector-fit behaves acceptably for slower edges, but fast-edge RX waveform error is still too large.
- **Cisco `.s4p` Ch10/Ch3**

  - `vector_3r3c` fails frequency fit gates.
  - No selected vector model yet.
  - Meaning: low-order full 4-port vector fitting is too weak for these channels.
- **`dc_hold` preprocessing**

  - Did not help in this pilot.
  - For Clarity it made things worse: non-passive / dense singular value / group-delay failure.
  - Meaning: simply prepending DC from the first frequency point is not a magic fix and may destabilize the fit.

**Main Finding**

Reduced models still look better for the scoped RX-through 50 ohm task.

But we still have **not** exhausted vector fitting. What we have shown is:

```text
vector_3r3c + raw/dc_hold is insufficient
```

not:

```text
vector fitting cannot work
```

**Why this matters**

The result matches our broader observation: frequency-domain vector fitting can produce a valid-looking `.sp`, but fast-edge transient correlation is the real test. The Clarity case is especially useful because it passes at `500 ps` but fails at `5 ps` and `50 ps`, which tells us the weakness is high-frequency/edge behavior, not basic connectivity.

**Next Steps**

1. Run a broader vector-fit sweep on the same pilot cases:

   - `vector_5r5c`
   - `vector_8r8c`
   - `vector_10r10c`
   - `vector_12r12c`
   - `lin` and `log` pole spacing
   - raw and frequency-trim variants
2. Prioritize `.s4p` full-vector fitting:

   - The current low-order fit failed Cisco channels.
   - We need to see whether higher order or trimming can recover a full 4-port model.
3. Compare preprocessing:

   - Keep `raw`.
   - Keep `dc_hold`, but treat cautiously.
   - Try `freq_trim_0p9` and `freq_trim_0p75`, because fast-edge failure may be tied to noisy/high-frequency fit behavior.
4. Run HSPICE audit only on selected candidates:

   - Do not audit every failed candidate.
   - First select by independent frequency/passivity/smoke metrics.
   - Then audit the best vector-fit candidates.
5. Add vector-fit vs reduced comparison figures:

   - For Clarity: HSPICE vs ngspice vector-fit, and HSPICE vs ngspice reduced model.
   - For Cisco: reduced currently works better for RX shape; vector-fit needs a higher-order attempt.

The immediate practical next command is the full pilot sweep, not the full dataset yet. Full dataset will be expensive.

Done. I completed the expanded scikit-rf vector-fit pilot: fit sweep, ngspice smoke, HSPICE audit, report regeneration, and a new findings note.

Main result: vector fitting is **not ready as the general full-model path yet**.

- `232` vector-fit candidates tested.
- Only `2` passed frequency/passivity gates, both for Clarity raw `vector_3r3c_lin`.
- Both Cisco `.s4p` pilot cases failed before simulation on S-matrix fit quality.
- After ngspice smoke, Clarity downgraded to `WARN`.
- HSPICE confirmed the warning:
  - `5 ps`: FAIL, RX RMSE `47.15 mV`, max error `196.67 mV`
  - `50 ps`: FAIL, RX RMSE `23.35 mV`, max error `98.34 mV`
  - `500 ps`: PASS, RX RMSE `6.42 mV`, max error `19.63 mV`

So the finding is: **plain full S-matrix vector fitting can look excellent in frequency domain but still fail fast-edge transient correlation.** It works better for slower edges, but it is not enough for sharp digital transitions yet.

You’re probably seeing ignored generated files, not uncommitted changes.

I checked Git after the push:

```powershell
git status --short
```

is empty, and:

```powershell
git status -sb
```

shows:

```text
## main...origin/main
```

So tracked changes are committed and pushed.

The “lots of U and M” you’re seeing are likely from VS Code decorations over simulator outputs and ignored files. When I ran:

```powershell
git status --short --ignored
```

Git showed thousands of `!!` ignored files, mostly `*.raw`, `*.log`, `__MACOSX`, and dependency/cache folders. Those are intentionally ignored and will not be committed or pushed.

In short:

- `M` would mean modified tracked file, but Git currently reports none.
- `U` in VS Code often means untracked, but Git currently reports zero untracked non-ignored files.
- The remaining clutter is ignored local generated data from ngspice/HSPICE runs.

To verify clean state yourself:

```powershell
git status --short
```

If that prints nothing, you’re clean. Use this only if you want to see the ignored clutter:

```powershell
git status --short --ignored
```

> ok so we can use the BBS CLI to convert sNp to sp successfully?

Yes. For the tested case, the BBS CLI successfully converts Touchstone `sNp` to SPICE netlists.

Confirmed with `Clarity_example.S2P`:

- HSPICE-compatible output: `*_BBSckt.txt`
- General SPICE-compatible output: `*_GSPICE.txt`
- The generated General SPICE model also ran in ngspice in a small transient smoke test.

So the practical answer is: yes, we can use this BBS CLI as a Touchstone-to-SPICE conversion path.

Important caveat: we have only verified one `.s2p` so far. Next we should test `.s4p` channels, especially Cisco/Molex, and compare BBS-generated ngspice results against HSPICE native S-parameter results. That will tell us whether BBS is just “convertible” or actually a better production path for our ngspice workflow.

> Plan
>
> # BBS S-Parameter Conversion Integration Plan
>
> ## Summary
>
> Add Cadence/Sigrity Broadband SPICE as a first-class conversion path in the existing S-parameter trust workflow. For every supported Touchstone channel, generate both BBS HSPICE-compatible and BBS General SPICE outputs, smoke-test the General SPICE output in ngspice, audit against native HSPICE S-element results, and compare BBS quality against the current scikit-rf vector-fit and reduced-model flows.
>
> Canonical output folder:
>
> `results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16`
>
> ## Key Changes
>
> - Add a repo-local BBS wrapper at `scripts/bbs_extract.py` based on the tested CLI from `C:\Users\sh3qm\code\BBS\bbs_extract.py`.
>
>   - Preserve existing CLI options: `input`, `--mode`, `--circuit-type`, `--max-iter`, `--freq`, `--error`, `--config`, `--init-config`, `--exe`.
>   - Keep the fixed output detection: HSPICE expects `*_BBSckt.txt`; General SPICE expects `*_GSPICE.txt`.
>   - Add a machine-readable summary file per run, e.g. `bbs_manifest.csv`, recording input file, mode, circuit type, output file, exit status, generated files, and BroadbandSPICE executable path.
>   - Do not require tuning by default; clean extraction remains the baseline.
> - Integrate BBS into `scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py` as a candidate family.
>
>   - New candidate families:
>     - `bbs_passivity2_hspice`
>     - `bbs_passivity2_gspice`
>     - `bbs_precision_hspice`
>     - `bbs_precision_gspice`
>   - V1 default candidate grid:
>     - `mode=passivity2`, `mode=precision`
>     - `circuit-type=hspice` and `circuit-type=gspice` for both modes
>     - `max-iter=200`
>     - no tuning config
>   - BBS candidates are full-model candidates, not reduced RX-only models.
>   - ngspice simulation uses the `*_GSPICE.txt` model.
>   - HSPICE reference/deployment output uses the `*_BBSckt.txt` model.
>   - HSPICE audit remains native S-element from the original Touchstone vs ngspice using BBS General SPICE; HSPICE audit must not influence selection.
> - Add BBS-specific outputs to the study folder.
>
>   - `bbs_candidates.csv`: one row per channel/mode/circuit-type.
>   - `bbs_ngspice_smoke.csv`: ngspice transient sanity for BBS General SPICE models.
>   - `bbs_hspice_correlation.csv`: native HSPICE Touchstone vs ngspice BBS General SPICE correlation.
>   - `selected_models/bbs/`: copied BBS HSPICE and General SPICE netlists for chosen cases.
>   - `plots/bbs_overlays/`: RX and TX HSPICE-vs-ngspice overlays.
>   - `README.md`: BBS summary table beside scikit-rf vector-fit and reduced-model results.
>
> ## Workflow
>
> - Phase 1: BBS pilot on representative channels.
>
>   - Run on:
>     - `hspice/sparam/Clarity_example.S2P`
>     - `hspice/sparam/Molex2006-2_T.s4p`
>     - Cisco `Ch10_35_5F3N_f4.s4p`
>     - Cisco `Ch3_17_5F3N_f3.s4p`
>   - Generate both HSPICE and General SPICE outputs for `passivity2` and `precision`.
>   - Run ngspice smoke on every General SPICE output.
>   - Run HSPICE native S-element audit for the same transient cases.
>   - Produce one clean RX plot and one clean TX plot per channel/mode.
> - Phase 2: BBS vs existing workflows.
>
>   - Compare BBS against:
>     - current scikit-rf vector-fit selected model
>     - current reduced RX-through selected model
>     - native HSPICE S-element reference
>   - Report separately:
>     - RX voltage shape
>     - RX timing confidence
>     - TX/reflection behavior
>     - full-model readiness
>   - BBS may receive `FULL_MODEL_READY` only if it passes full-model gates; reduced `.s4p` remains scoped and cannot receive full-model readiness.
> - Phase 3: Batch run.
>
>   - Run BBS conversion on all supported `.s2p` / `.s4p` channels from:
>     - repo-local `hspice/sparam`
>     - Cisco channels
>     - Molex
>     - fetched scikit-rf fixtures
>   - Use `passivity2` as the baseline mode.
>   - Include `precision` only for pilot failures or selected representative channels to control runtime.
>   - Generate final report showing where BBS is better, worse, or complementary.
>
> ## Metrics And Classification
>
> - Reuse existing independent metrics:
>
>   - ngspice run success
>   - finite waveform values
>   - transient voltage bounds
>   - RX active-window RMSE/max error
>   - TX active-window RMSE/max error
>   - 50% delay only when threshold confidence is high
>   - overshoot/undershoot
>   - settling
>   - pre-response sanity
> - Add BBS-specific checks:
>
>   - output file exists for both HSPICE and General SPICE
>   - General SPICE subcircuit parses in ngspice
>   - HSPICE-compatible subcircuit is generated and archived
>   - BBS fitted Touchstone output, if present, is archived and optionally compared against original Touchstone
>   - `Error_Order.txt` is captured and summarized
> - Classification:
>
>   - `BBS_NGSPICE_READY`: General SPICE output runs in ngspice and passes independent transient gates.
>   - `BBS_HSPICE_READY`: HSPICE-compatible output is generated and syntactically present.
>   - `BBS_FULL_MODEL_READY`: BBS ngspice result passes full-model independent gates and HSPICE audit correlation.
>   - `BBS_WARN`: conversion works but has named caveats, such as RX timing ambiguity, TX mismatch, or mode-specific extraction warning.
>   - `BBS_FAIL`: conversion missing, ngspice parse failure, unstable/nonfinite transient, or severe waveform violation.
>
> ## Commands
>
> - Pilot conversion and audit:
>
>   ```powershell
>   py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py qualify `
>     --study-dir results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16 `
>     --extra-touchstone-dir hspice/sparam `
>     --enable-bbs `
>     --bbs-modes passivity2,precision `
>     --bbs-circuit-types hspice,gspice `
>     --dense-samples 501 `
>     --sim-timeout 180
>   ```
> - HSPICE audit:
>
>   ```powershell
>   py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py audit-hspice `
>     --study-dir results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16 `
>     --sim-timeout 240 `
>     --audit-stop-ns 35 `
>     --max-channels 20 `
>     --resume
>   ```
> - Report:
>
>   ```powershell
>   py -3.14 scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py report `
>     --study-dir results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16
>   ```
>
> ## Test Plan
>
> - Unit-style checks:
>
>   - `scripts/bbs_extract.py --help` works.
>   - `--init-config` writes valid JSON.
>   - HSPICE output detection recognizes `*_BBSckt.txt`.
>   - General SPICE output detection recognizes `*_GSPICE.txt`.
>   - Missing BroadbandSPICE executable produces a clear error.
>   - Candidate selection does not read HSPICE correlation files.
> - Integration checks:
>
>   - `Clarity_example.S2P` produces both HSPICE and General SPICE BBS netlists.
>   - Generated General SPICE model runs in ngspice with a 50-ohm source/load smoke deck.
>   - `.s4p` Cisco/Molex channels produce BBS outputs or explicit failures.
>   - Every accepted BBS General SPICE model has ngspice `.raw` and `.log`.
>   - Every audited BBS case has HSPICE `.tr0`/`.lis` and overlay plots.
>   - README clearly compares BBS, scikit-rf vector-fit, and reduced RX-through results.
> - Acceptance criteria:
>
>   - At least one `.s2p` and one `.s4p` complete the full BBS conversion plus ngspice smoke path.
>   - At least four representative channels have RX and TX HSPICE-vs-ngspice overlays.
>   - The report clearly states whether BBS is currently production-promising, only experimental, or failing for each channel family.
>   - No BBS model is marked `FULL_MODEL_READY` unless it passes full-model gates.
>
> ## Assumptions
>
> - BroadbandSPICE executable default:
>   `C:\Cadence\Sigrity2024.1\tools\bin\BroadbandSPICE.exe`
> - BBS is integrated as a first-class candidate family, not just a manual CLI.
> - Both HSPICE-compatible and General SPICE outputs are required deliverables.
> - ngspice uses the BBS General SPICE output.
> - HSPICE audit uses native HSPICE S-element from the original Touchstone as the reference.
> - Clean, untuned BBS extraction is the baseline; tuning configs are future experiments.
> - HSPICE remains audit-only and never changes qualification selection.

</details>

The main decision that materially changes the plan is whether BBS becomes a first-class conversion path in our existing trust workflow, or stays as a separate comparison campaign until it proves itself. I have a recommended default, but I want to lock that before writing the official plan.

> explain in detail, what's done

Implemented BBS as a real conversion path in our existing S-parameter workflow.

**What Was Added**
Added a repo-local BBS wrapper:

[scripts/bbs_extract.py](/c:/Users/sh3qm/code/ibis_comparison/scripts/bbs_extract.py)

This wraps Cadence/Sigrity BroadbandSPICE batch mode:

```powershell
BroadbandSPICE.exe -b -NoUI -py generated_script.py
```

It supports:

```text
input
--mode passivity/passivity2/passivity3/passivity4/precision
--circuit-type hspice/gspice/spectre
--max-iter
--freq
--error
--config
--init-config
--manifest
--exe
--timeout
```

Important fix: BBS writes different output names depending on circuit type:

- HSPICE output: `*_BBSckt.txt`
- General SPICE output: `*_GSPICE.txt`

The wrapper now detects both correctly.

**What Was Integrated**
Updated:

[scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py](/c:/Users/sh3qm/code/ibis_comparison/scripts/run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py)

New command options include:

```powershell
--enable-bbs
--bbs-exe
--bbs-modes
--bbs-circuit-types
--bbs-max-iter
--bbs-error
--bbs-config
--bbs-timeout
```

When `--enable-bbs` is used, the workflow now:

1. Copies the Touchstone into a per-channel BBS work folder.
2. Runs BBS extraction for HSPICE and General SPICE.
3. Archives generated BBS files.
4. Wraps the BBS General SPICE subckt as `s_equivalent`, so existing ngspice testbenches can use it.
5. Runs ngspice smoke tests on the BBS General SPICE model.
6. Optionally runs HSPICE native S-element audit against ngspice+BBS.
7. Reports BBS separately in the README and CSV outputs.

**New Output Files**
In the study folder, BBS now creates:

```text
bbs_candidates.csv
bbs_ngspice_smoke.csv
bbs_hspice_correlation.csv
selected_models/bbs/
plots/bbs_overlays/
```

Canonical result folder:

[results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16](/c:/Users/sh3qm/code/ibis_comparison/results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16)

The report is here:

[README.md](/c:/Users/sh3qm/code/ibis_comparison/results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_2026-06-16/README.md)

**What Was Tested**
I ran a canonical BBS pilot with:

- `Clarity_example.S2P`
- `Agilent_E5071B.s4p`

For each, BBS generated:

- one HSPICE-compatible model
- one General SPICE model

The General SPICE models then ran in ngspice smoke tests.

Smoke output summary:

- BBS extraction rows: `4`
- BBS HSPICE-compatible outputs: `2`
- BBS General SPICE outputs: `2`
- BBS ngspice smoke rows: `24`
- BBS HSPICE audit rows: `2`

**Current Finding**
Mechanically, the flow works: BBS can convert Touchstone to SPICE, and the General SPICE output can run in ngspice.

But quality-wise, the tested BBS models are not yet trusted full-model replacements. In the canonical run:

```text
BBS independent PASS/WARN/FAIL: 0 / 0 / 2
BBS HSPICE audit P/W/F/E:       0 / 0 / 2 / 0
```

So both BBS candidates converted and simulated, but failed the current quality gates.

That is actually useful: now BBS is in the same comparison framework as scikit-rf vector fitting and reduced models, so we can judge it with the same metrics.

**Important Extra Finding**
Cisco large `.s4p` BBS extraction was slow enough to exceed the test budget. I added `--bbs-timeout`, so instead of hanging the whole batch, the workflow records explicit timeout failures in `bbs_candidates.csv`.

Example result folder:

[results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_s4p_timeout_smoke_2026-06-16](/c:/Users/sh3qm/code/ibis_comparison/results/sparam_bbs_integration_v1_s4p_timeout_smoke_2026-06-16)

So now we can safely batch BBS over larger datasets without getting stuck forever on one channel.

**Bottom Line**
We now have BBS as a first-class conversion candidate in the workflow.

It can:

- convert `.sNp` to SPICE,
- produce both HSPICE and General SPICE files,
- run General SPICE in ngspice,
- compare against native HSPICE S-element,
- generate reports and overlays.

The next step is not “make it run” anymore. That part is done. The next step is to evaluate/tune BBS settings and decide whether BBS gives better correlation than scikit-rf vector fitting or reduced models for the channel families we care about.

> Plan
>
> # BBS Quality Tuning and Comparison Campaign
>
> ## Summary
>
> Build the next BBS study around quality tuning, not just conversion success. The current integration proves BBS can generate HSPICE and General SPICE models and that ngspice can run the General SPICE output, but the first clean `passivity2` BBS models failed independent quality gates and HSPICE audit on the tested `.s2p`/`.s4p` cases. The next deliverable will be a clear comparison report showing whether BBS tuning can improve correlation versus scikit-rf vector fitting and reduced RX-through models.
>
> Canonical output folder:
>
> `results/sparam_bbs_quality_tuning_v1_2026-06-17`
>
> ## Key Changes
>
> - Extend the BBS workflow with named global tuning presets.
>
>   - Add `--bbs-preset-grid clean,reciprocity,lowfreq,smoothing,causality,recip_lowfreq,smooth_lowfreq`.
>   - Each preset writes a JSON config under `inputs/bbs_configs/` and records exact options in `bbs_candidates.csv`.
>   - Keep `clean` as the baseline; no per-channel hand tuning.
>   - Do not enable risky DC-file or interpolation presets in v1 unless they pass a standalone API smoke test.
> - Expand BBS candidate identity and reporting.
>
>   - Candidate names should include mode, circuit type, and preset, for example `bbs_passivity2_gspice_clean`.
>   - Generate both HSPICE and General SPICE for every BBS candidate.
>   - Use General SPICE for ngspice smoke/audit.
>   - Archive both BBS netlists under `selected_models/bbs/<channel>/<candidate>/`.
>   - Preserve BBS timeout/failure rows so large channels are explicit failures, not silent skips.
> - Add BBS-focused comparison outputs.
>
>   - `bbs_candidates.csv`: extraction status, mode, circuit type, preset, timeout, output files.
>   - `bbs_metrics.csv`: BBS-only independent metrics copied from `metrics.csv`.
>   - `bbs_ngspice_smoke.csv`: transient smoke rows for BBS General SPICE models.
>   - `bbs_hspice_correlation.csv`: native HSPICE S-element vs ngspice+BBS.
>   - `bbs_ranking.csv`: best BBS candidate per channel by independent score only.
>   - `plots/bbs_overlays/`: one RX plot and one TX plot per audited case.
>   - README section comparing BBS, scikit-rf vector fit, and reduced model for each representative channel.
> - Improve visual comparison.
>
>   - Generate clean one-plot-per-figure RX and TX overlays for BBS vs native HSPICE.
>   - Use unified voltage-axis increments so small mV errors do not look exaggerated.
>   - Add side-by-side summary tables with RMSE, max error, delay delta, and pass/warn/fail class.
>   - Include the exact BBS `.sp`/`.txt` model and testbench used for each representative plotted case.
>
> ## Experiment Plan
>
> - Phase 1: API/preset smoke.

> ## Assumptions
>
> - Primary goal is quality tuning and comparison evidence.
> - The visible deliverable is a comparison report with clean plots.
> - BBS remains a first-class candidate family, not a replacement for scikit-rf or reduced models yet.
> - HSPICE remains audit-only and never changes independent candidate selection.
> - Clean BBS extraction remains the baseline; tuning presets are global and reproducible.

</details>

Current truth is pretty crisp: BBS conversion is integrated and mechanically works for `.s2p` plus at least one `.s4p`, but the first clean `passivity2` models fail quality/audit gates; large Cisco `.s4p` can exceed a reasonable extraction budget. The next plan needs to decide whether tomorrow’s value is “find better BBS settings,” “broaden evidence,” or “optimize runtime,” because those pull the implementation in different directions.

Correct, that overnight command does **not** use BBS / Broadband SPICE.

It runs the **scikit-rf VectorFitting path only**:

- input: original Touchstone `.s2p` / `.s4p`
- conversion: scikit-rf vector fitting exported to ngspice-compatible `.sp`
- ngspice smoke test: converted `.sp`
- HSPICE audit: native HSPICE S-element using the original Touchstone
- comparison: ngspice converted model vs HSPICE native Touchstone result

So it is testing:

```text
Touchstone
   -> scikit-rf VectorFitting
   -> exported SPICE macromodel
   -> ngspice
   vs
Touchstone
   -> HSPICE native S-element
```

BBS is part of the other broader trust workflow script, `run_sparam_conversion_quality_study.py`, but not this dedicated vector-fitting campaign.

Yes and no.

For a **small pilot**, fitting/evaluation should be fairly quick. But the command I gave is the **full exhaustive vector-fit campaign**, and that is much heavier than our reduced-model flow.

Current run is doing:

```text
207 supported channels
x 4 preprocessing modes
x 21 vector-fit candidates
= up to 17,388 vector-fit attempts
```

Most of those are `.s4p` channels, so each fit is a full 4-port / 16-S-parameter rational model. The slow parts are:

- scikit-rf `VectorFitting` iterative solves
- `auto_fit_tight` / `auto_fit_very_tight`
- high-order fixed fits like `10r10c` and `12r12c`
- passivity checks / dense singular-value evaluation
- SPICE export and fit plots

So the **frequency evaluation itself** is not the slow part. The **full vector-fit sweep** is.

Right now it is active, not stuck. It has started processing channels and is currently in the full `fit` phase. It has not reached ngspice or HSPICE yet.
